incident-bot: ALERT: Hosted API latency SLO violation detected in us-west-2 — p99 > 2500ms across multiple services. Triggered at 2024-03-13T21:48:43Z. paging oncall @here

Sara Patel: saw the page, jumping in. initial numbers?

incident-bot: Summary metrics (rolling 5m): hosted-text-generate p95=420ms (baseline ~120ms), p99=2600ms (baseline ~300ms). Streaming stall rate increased to 4.7% (was <0.2%). Errors: 502s still low, most are long tail latency/timeouts.

Mike Chen: adding early hypothesis — we rolled runtime kernels last night (PR #4820, runtime/kernel-selection) that included new FlashAttention/TRT kernel paths and a new compiler flag set: nvcc -O3 --use_fast_math + custom kernel fusion. Deployed 03/12 02:13 UTC.

Anika Rao: correlating traces now — I see spike aligns with the kernel rollout window. The decode latency heatmap shows tail concentrated on streaming endpoints and long sequence lengths (seq_len > 1024).

Kevin O'Neill: logs from a stalled stream: 
```
[2024-03-13T21:46:12Z] req_id=abc123 decode_latency_ms=1580 kernel=flash_attn_v2 worker_id=wm-07
[2024-03-13T21:46:12Z] req_id=abc123 stall_point=kv_cache_fetch duration_ms=1200
[2024-03-13T21:46:13Z] req_id=def456 decode_latency_ms=2300 kernel=trt_fused_attn worker_id=wm-03
```

Sara Patel: thanks. sounds like new kernels (flash_attn_v2 / trt_fused_attn) are regressing tail. Can we switch fallback kernel selection at runtime?

Julian Park: kernel selection is dynamic but the new code added an aggressive selection policy that prefers fused kernels for speed — and apparently they regress for certain shapes. I can push a runtime flag to prefer legacy kernels per model.

Mike Chen: short-term mitigation options: 1) flip runtime config to prefer legacy kernels (cheap, immediate), 2) rollback PR and redeploy runtime (longer), 3) pin affected worker pool to previous container image (canary restart).

Anika Rao: customer impact: estimate ~3% of requests experience high tail latency. Affected customers: streaming users with >1k seq and batch sizes of 1. No widespread 5xx; mostly stalls and slow streaming chunk arrivals. Recommend notifying CS for top-tier customers on Dedicated and Private.

Sara Patel: immediate action: flip runtime flag to prefer legacy kernels for us-west-2. Who can make the config change? Also trigger routing policy to divert streaming traffic to fallback smaller model (if possible) to relieve pressure.

Kevin O'Neill: I can flip the flag. patch: 
```
# runtime config: /etc/redwood/runtime.conf
kernel_selection_policy=compatibility_first
```
Applying to worker pool: `kubectl patch deployment runtime-wm --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"kernel_policy":"compatibility_first"}}}}}' -n prod-us-west-2`

deploy-bot: rolling update started for deployment/runtime-wm (us-west-2) — 12 pods to update. 3 pods updated so far.

Mike Chen: also enabling a streaming circuit-breaker to limit max_concurrent_streams per worker to 20 (was 50) to reduce contention on KV cache.

Sara Patel: good. Julian/Anika, once flag flips, watch p95/p99 and streaming stall metric. set alert thresholds to catch refires.

Anika Rao: post-change snapshot 2m after flip: p95=140ms, p99=420ms, streaming stalls down to 0.6%. Significant improvement.

Sara Patel: that's promising. keep an eye for 10m. Rolling update looks healthy so far.

Julian Park: we should still do a controlled rollback of the kernel selection PR in staging and add more regression tests (long sequences + batch_size=1 + streaming). My suspicion: fusion path causes extra mem pressure and bad scheduling on certain GPUs causing stalls.

Mike Chen: agreed. next steps for root cause: build repro harness to run seq_len 1024..4096 with model X and both kernel variants; profile kernel runtime and CUDA occupancy. I'll coordinate with infra to pin a node with same GPU type.

Kevin O'Neill: for immediate customer comms, we should prepare a short note: impacted customers (streaming-heavy) saw degraded streaming chunk latency, partial mitigation applied, follow-up postmortem in 48h. Assign CS owner?

Sara Patel: @Julian will own the postmortem & repro. @Mike will own builds and profiling. @Anika will own metric/alert updates. @Kevin please coordinate CS comms. I'll remain oncall until handoff at 02:00 UTC.

deploy-bot: rolling update completed for deployment/runtime-wm (us-west-2). 12/12 pods updated.

Anika Rao: 10m steady-state after fix: p95=130ms, p99=310ms, streaming stalls 0.2% — back to near baseline. No customer escalations yet.

Mike Chen: build notes — the problematic compiler flags were a new nvcc flag and an extra kernel fusion pass. I have a local build with the fusion disabled; initial unit profile shows tail latency reduction. Will run full repro.

Julian Park: adding to action item list:
- Revert or harden PR #4820 (kernel selection)
- Add long-tail streaming e2e tests in CI
- Add failure-mode tests for kernel_fusion flag combinations
- Improve rollout gating for kernel-level changes (canary across GPU families)

Kevin O'Neill: CS note draft: 
"We observed short-lived increases in streaming response latency in us-west-2. We applied an immediate mitigation that restored normal latency; engineering is investigating a kernel-level regression introduced in a recent runtime change. We will follow up with a postmortem and timeline within 48 hours."

Sara Patel: final status for now: incident mitigated by runtime config flip and circuit-breaker. Root cause suspected: new kernel fusion/TRT kernel paths regress tail for specific shapes. Postmortem owners assigned. Closing page, will reopen if metrics regress.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: SLOs restored in us-west-2. Duration: ~1h10m.

Mike Chen: follow-up: I'll open a revert PR for the kernel-selection change with a plan to reintroduce behind safer canary gates. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4892

Julian Park: I'll start the repro harness and will post logs in this thread when ready.

Kevin O'Neill: tagging CS for follow-up: @support-team. Thanks everyone.

Sara Patel: handing off oncall to Mike Chen now. `handoff: Sara -> Mike (02:00 UTC)` — Mike, please ack.

Mike Chen: ack, taking over oncall.

Anika Rao: quick note for the postmortem: include exact GPU types impacted (A100 v3 on that pool), kernel versions, nvcc flags, and commit ids. Also include a timeline of metric regression.

Julian Park: noted. posting initial repro artifacts here when done.

Sara Patel: thanks team. good coordination. :thumbsup:
